statement: Let $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$ be two circles of unequal radii with centres $O_1$ and $O_2$, intersecting at two distinct points $A$ and $B$. The centre of each circle is outside the other. The tangent to $\Gamma_1$ at $B$ meets $\Gamma_2$ again at $C$ (different from $B$); the tangent to $\Gamma_2$ at $B$ meets $\Gamma_1$ again at $D$ (different from $B$). The bisectors of $\angle DAB$ and $\angle CAB$ meet $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$ again at $X$ and $Y$ respectively. Let $P$ and $Q$ be the circumcentres of triangles $ACD$ and $XAY$. Prove that $PQ$ is the perpendicular bisector of the segment $O_1O_2$.

Suppose $P(x)$ is a polynomial with real coefficients satisfying $P(\cos\theta + \sin\theta) = P(\cos\theta - \sin\theta)$ for every real $\theta$. Prove that $P(x)$ can be expressed in the form $P(x) = a_0 + a_1(1-x^2)^2 + a_2(1-x^2)^4 + \cdots + a_n(1-x^2)^{2n}$ for some real numbers $a_0, a_1, \ldots, a_n$ and nonneg­ative integer $n$.

Let $S$ be a subset of $\{0,1,2,\ldots,9\}$. Suppose there is a positive integer $N$ such that for any integer $n > N$, one can find positive integers $a, b$ with $n = a + b$ and all digits of $a$ and $b$ (in their decimal representations, without leading zeros) belonging to $S$. Find the smallest possible value of $|S|$.

Let $n \geq 2$ be an integer and let $1 < a_1 \leq a_2 \leq \cdots \leq a_n$ be real numbers with $a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_n = 2n$. Prove that $a_1 a_2 \cdots a_{n-1} + a_1 a_2 \cdots a_{n-2} + \cdots + a_1 a_2 + a_1 + 2 \leq a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n$.

Infinitely many equidistant parallel lines are drawn in the plane. A positive integer $n \geq 3$ is called frameable if it is possible to draw a regular polygon with $n$ sides such that all vertices lie on these lines and no line contains more than one vertex. (a) Show that $3, 4, 6$ are frameable. (b) Show that any integer $n \geq 7$ is not frameable. (c) Determine whether $5$ is frameable.

A stromino is a $3 \times 1$ rectangle. Show that a $5 \times 5$ board divided into twenty-five $1 \times 1$ squares cannot be covered by 16 strominos such that each stromino covers exactly three squares of the board and every square is covered by one or two strominos. (A stromino can be placed horizontally or vertically.)
